messages:
maya: heads up — seeing NVMe IOPS throttle + GPU attach backlog in us-east1 after a BGP flap ~09:11 UTC. :rotating_light:

Logs from hot node (sample):
```
2026-03-21T09:11:08Z nvme14 iops=45230 write_lat=12.3ms scrub_jobs=6
2026-03-21T09:11:09Z nvme15 iops=46780 write_lat=13.1ms scrub_jobs=7
2026-03-21T09:11:10Z gpu-scheduler attach_queue=126 pending=18
```

kai: saw it too. grafana shows scratchpool iops spike + scrub jobs all firing at once. gpu queue +120. :eyes:

otto: logs indicate metadata sync storms — several nodes re-fetching shards after peer failover, lots of short-lived TCP connections to the same rack pair.

maya: routing change moved traffic onto a single backup peer for the region, looks like affinity concentrated on racks 7-9.

jen: can we pause cleaner/scrub jobs? tradeoff: temporary higher backlog vs starving GPUs.

maya: going to scale janitor down now: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy/ephemeral-janitor --replicas=0`

maya: executed — will report if IOPS drops.

deploy-bot: [automated] scaled deployment ephemeral-janitor -> 0 (triggered by maya)
messages_continued:
aaron: IOPS dropped from ~45k -> ~8k on the hot nodes within 90s. gpu attach queue reduced by ~40% so far.

kai: good. we should throttle background compaction on those hosts and avoid global sysctl changes.

otto: quick per-node tweak suggestion: reduce cleaner concurrency and lower dirty_ratio locally. e.g. `sysctl -w vm.dirty_ratio=5` and restart cleaner with --concurrency=2.

jen: prefer do this via a systemd drop-in or daemonset patch not manual sysctl. i'll push a safe per-node change.

maya: routing pinged netops for a weighted fix — @marta can we spread backup peer across multiple upstreams?

marta: initiating weighted failover now, spreading across three peers instead of single. ETA ~8m.

sre-watch: health check: no file-level corruption detected (all zero errs). heatmap shows wear concentration on nvme14/15 subset; wear not related to corruption this round.

aaron: operational plan: keep janitor scaled to 0 for 30m, monitor iops and gpu queue; when stable, re-enable janitor with env RATE_LIMIT=200 and concurrency lowered.

maya: re-enable plan prepared: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy/ephemeral-janitor --replicas=2 && kubectl -n infra set env deploy/ephemeral-janitor RATE_LIMIT=200`. will only do after sustained low IOPS.

kai: noted. will follow up with a postmortem focusing on: BGP peer weighting + scratchpool affinity causing hot-routing + missing hot-node alarms.

jen: finance ask: any cost impact from cross-rack egress during the failover?

maya: rough estimate from billing logs: ~ $1,200 in extra egress for the incident window (tallies are preliminary).

aaron: GPUs recovered; attach wait times are back to normal. i'll watch for 30m then re-enable full scrub cadence gradually.

maya: thanks team :thumbsup:

otto: follow-ups I'll add to infra board: [ ] peer-weight safety guard, [ ] per-region scrub rate caps, [ ] hot-node detection alarms + auto-mitigations.

maya: closing thread unless someone sees new anomalies.
